approved: Treasury Laws Amendment (2020 Measures No. 1) Bill 2020

The majority voted in favour of keeping the second reading motion unchanged. A [second reading motion](https://peo.gov.au/understand-our-parliament/how-parliament-works/bills-and-laws/making-a-law-in-the-australian-parliament/) is a motion to agree with the main idea of the bill. This vote was put after the MP for Whitlam [Stephen Jones](https://theyvoteforyou.org.au/people/representatives/whitlam/stephen_jones) proposed the following amendment: > *That all words after "That" be omitted with a view to substituting the following words:* > > *"whilst not declining to give the bill a second reading, the House:* > > *(1) calls on the Government to commit to the legislated increase of the superannuation guarantee to 12 per cent; and* > > *(2) notes that the Government's failure to make sure multinationals pay their fair share of tax in Australia is weakening our economy".*
The speaker announced they will formally move an amendment to the Treasury Laws Amendment (2020 Measures No. 1) Bill 2020 at the conclusion of their contribution.

The speaker argued in support of the Treasury Laws Amendment (2020 Measures No. 1) Bill 2020 without the amendment, stating it promotes tax integrity by ensuring people and corporations meet their tax obligations while providing appropriate relief for superannuation funds.

The second reading amendment to raise superannuation to 12% was supported, and the bill’s multinational tax measures were criticised as a wholly inadequate step, with up to $240 billion in OECD tax bases under threat from profit shifting.

The speaker supported the second reading amendment moved by the member for Whitlam, arguing it addresses trust and economic impacts on superannuation, and urged government members to support it, citing $13 billion in revenue from cracking down on tax avoidance.

The speaker supported the second reading amendment criticising the government's multinational tax transparency approach and called for committing to the staged superannuation guarantee increase to 12%. They argued the bill's measures expanding the definition of significant global entities and making super fund merger tax relief permanent are insufficient, noting that 710 of 2,214 companies examined paid no tax in 2017-18, including 102 with over $1 billion in income.

The speaker argued that multinational profit-shifting to tax havens costs the global economy $600 billion annually and Australia over $100 billion in assets, criticising the Coalition for cutting ATO staff, weakening tax transparency, and failing to lead on OECD initiatives like Tax Inspectors Without Borders, which yields $100 per dollar spent.

The speaker argued that multinational tax avoidance costs Australia billions, with $8.7 trillion globally sheltered in tax havens and a $109 billion Australian tax gap, and called for stronger multilateral action beyond the current bill's redefinition of significant global entities.
